content:
In *Fallout 76*, **Legendary items** are weapons, armor, and power armor that have 1 or more **Legendary mods** slotted into them. Legendary items are identified by one or more stars (★) in their names where the number of stars are determined by the number of slotted Legendary mods for that item. These Legendary mods provide stat bonuses to the item or character or other special effects that typically trigger in combat.

Legendary items may drop as loot from Legendary enemies, be purchased from Purveyor Murmrgh, or be rewarded from events, quests, Daily Ops, or Expeditions. Additionally, Legendary crafting provides the ability to add Legendary mods to a non-Legendary item, craft Legendary mods and slot them into a Legendary item, and craft unique Legendary items with predetermined configurations of Legendary mods.

For detailed information on the Legendary mods available to each type of item, see the portal below:

| ![FO76 weapon 10mmpistol thumb](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/fallout/images/0/0a/FO76_weapon_10mmpistol_thumb.png) Ranged weapons | ![Fallout4 Combat knife](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/fallout/images/2/24/Fallout4_Combat_knife.png) Melee weapons | ![FO76 armor combatchestgo thumb](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/fallout/images/5/50/FO76_armor_combatchestgo_thumb.png) Armor | ![FO76 pa t51helm thumb](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/fallout/images/d/de/FO76_pa_t51helm_thumb.png) Power armor | 

Legendary items possess 1 or more Legendary mods and have a star rank equivalent to the number of these mods. These Legendary mods in turn have their own star ranks, equivalent to the 1 of 5 Legendary slots they are designed to fit into, e.g. Bloodied is a 1-star mod since it can only fit into the 1-star slot on a weapon. An item cannot simultaneously possess 2 or more mods in a specific slot, e.g. Explosive and Rapid are both 2-star weapon mods and the last to be attached to the weapon will overwrite the other.

The name of a Legendary item is prefixed by the name of its 1-star Legendary mod. In general, 2-star and 3-star mods do not change a Legendary item's name.

While 5-star mod slots are currently unused by randomly dropped or crafted items, they are occupied by custom mods used by various quest-specific unique legendary weapons and armors, such as Perfect Storm or All Rise.

| **Legendary item chance** | | 
| Category | Chance | 
| Melee weapon | 25% | 
| Ranged weapon | 25% | 
| Armor | 25% | 
| Power armor | 25% | 

A majority of the weapons in *Fallout 76* can be obtained as legendary items, however, there are a great many restrictions on what can and cannot appear as a legendary item.

Some items require the relevant plan to be learned before they can be obtained as legendary items from legendary enemies, crafting, the Purveyor, Daily Ops, events, quests, and expeditions. [bug 1] [bug 2] 

Some items cannot drop or be purchased from the Purveyor as legendary items, but may be turned into one by players using the legendary crafting system. These items will have to be crafted or obtained in the world as standard items and then converted into legendary items by rolling legendary mods at a workbench.

| **Legendary crafting only** | | | 
| Auto axe | Strangler heart power armor | The Invader | 

The following items may only obtained by turning in Pleasant Valley claim tickets to the Bellhop at Pleasant Valley Ski Resort. The fancy single action revolver will be rolled as a random 1-star legendary while the fancy pump action shotgun will drop with fixed 3-star effects.

| Pleasant Valley ticket claim only | | | 
| Fancy single action revolver | Fancy pump action shotgun | | 

The following weapons cannot exist as legendary items. No apparel, body suits or helmets can be rolled with legendary effects.

Raider power armor will always drop at 50% condition.

4-star legendary items were planned to be added in the *Invaders from Beyond* update, but were never released. *Gleaming Depths* reintroduces 4-star Legendary components as part of The Gleaming Depths raid.
